- Their ducts open at the lid margin to prevent tear evaporation.

category: Describe the histological structure of layers of eyeball, eyelid and retina
front: The thin, acellular, and highly refractile layer that serves as a modified basement membrane for the corneal endothelium is [___].
back:
- **Descemet’s Membrane**.
- It thickens with age (from 5 μm in infants to 17 μm in adults).
- Separates the corneal stroma from the endothelium.

category: Describe the histological structure of layers of eyeball, eyelid and retina
front: A diabetic patient presents with sudden vision loss. Histology reveals separation between the inner wall and outer wall of the embryonic optic cup. Name the two layers involved.
back:
- **Neural Retina** and **Retinal Pigment Epithelium** (RPE).
- This is **Retinal Detachment**.
- The neural retina loses metabolic support from the choroid and RPE.

category: Describe the histological structure of layers of eyeball, eyelid and retina
front: Specify the anatomical components of the Blood-Retina Barrier and how they facilitate immune privilege.
back:
- **Tight Junctions (Zonulae Occludentes)**: Between Retinal Pigment Epithelial (RPE) cells and between capillary endothelial cells.
- **Function**: Prevents toxic macromolecules and antigens from entering the neural retina.

category: Describe the histological structure of layers of eyeball, eyelid and retina
front: Distinguish between the synaptic terminations of Rods and Cones in the Outer Plexiform Layer.
back:
- **Rod Spherule**: The small, knob-like axonal ending of a rod cell.
- **Cone Pedicle**: The broad, expanded axonal ending of a cone cell.
- Synapse with **bipolar** and **horizontal** cell processes.

category: Describe the histological structure of layers of eyeball, eyelid and retina
front: Identify the three structural components of the Middle Vascular Coat (Uvea) from posterior to anterior.
back:
- **Choroid**: Highly vascular, dark brown layer.
- **Ciliary Body**: Triangular ring containing ciliary muscles/processes.
- **Iris**: Contractile diaphragm with central pupil.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: The specialized fluid that fills the scala media and is characterized by a high potassium concentration similar to intracellular fluid is [___].
back: * Endolymph * Secreted by the stria vascularis * Essential for creating the endocochlear potential

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: A 40-year-old patient presents with recurring episodes of dizziness, tinnitus, and a sensation of "fullness" in the ear. Identify the specific histological change in the membranous labyrinth.
back: * Endolymphatic hydrops * Overdistension of the membranous labyrinth * Caused by impaired drainage into the endolymphatic sac

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Explain the role of tip links in the hair bundle during the initiation of a nerve impulse in the Organ of Corti.
back: * Connect tips of shorter stereocilia to adjacent taller ones * Pull open mechanically-gated cation channels when hairs deflect * Facilitates rapid K+ influx from endolymph

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Contrast the pathological site of conductive hearing loss in otosclerosis with the site affected in sensorineural loss due to loud noise exposure.
back: * Otosclerosis: Abnormal bone deposition at the stapes footplate/oval window * Noise Exposure: Permanent damage to neuroepithelial hair cells in the Organ of Corti

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Identify the primary ion responsible for hair cell depolarization and explain why it moves into the cell despite its positive charge.
back: * Potassium (K+) * Moves down a steep electrochemical gradient from high-K+ endolymph * Influx triggers voltage-gated Ca2+ channels at the base

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
coreConcept: Supporting Cells of Organ of Corti
front: In the Organ of Corti, the neuroepithelial hair cells are supported by specialized columnar cells called [___] that rest on the basilar membrane and envelop the bases of outer hair cells.
back: * Outer phalangeal cells (Deiters cells) * Provide structural support via phalangeal processes * Contain abundant microtubules for structural rigidity

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Histological analysis of a fetal internal ear shows a failure of the ductus reuniens to form. Which two compartments of the membranous labyrinth would fail to communicate?
back: * Saccule * Cochlear duct (Scala media)

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Describe the structural differences between the apical hair bundles of the vestibular cristae and those of the auditory Organ of Corti.
back: * Cristae: Contain multiple stereocilia and one true kinocilium * Organ of Corti: Lack a kinocilium in mature cells; contain only stereocilia

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Distinguish the sensory function of the macula utriculi from that of the cristae ampullares.
back: * Macula utriculi: Detects linear acceleration and static head position (gravity) * Cristae ampullares: Detect angular acceleration (rotational movement)

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Name the acellular, gelatinous structure into which the stereocilia of the inner and outer hair cells are embedded.
back: * Tectorial membrane * Composed of type II and V collagen and glycoproteins * Attached medially to the limbus spiralis of the modiolus

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: The narrow membranous channel that provides direct communication between the saccule and the cochlear duct (scala media) is the [___].
back:
• Ductus reuniens
• Facilitates the continuous flow of endolymph within the membranous labyrinth.
• Essential for maintaining equalized pressure across different sensory regions.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: A researcher identifies specialized simple columnar cells with apical microvilli in a blind-ended sac of the internal ear. This sac is responsible for [___].
back:
• Absorption and drainage of endolymph
• Located in the endolymphatic sac.
• Ensures constant renewal and pressure regulation of the endolymphatic fluid.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Describe the histological composition of the Vestibular (Reissner's) membrane separating the scala media from the scala vestibuli.
back:
• Composed of a very thin connective tissue core.
• Covered on both surfaces by a single layer of simple squamous epithelium.
• Maintains the critical ionic gradient between endolymph and perilymph.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Contrast the location and morphological arrangement of Claudius cells versus Boettcher cells in the cochlear duct.
back:
• Claudius Cells: Cuboidal cells extending over the lateral basilar membrane.
• Boettcher Cells: Small polyhedral cells located deep to Claudius cells.
• Distribution: Boettcher cells are uniquely restricted to the basal turns.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Identify the specific cell type that provides primary structural support to the inner hair cells by completely surrounding their basal and lateral surfaces.
back:
• Inner phalangeal cells
• Flask-shaped cells resting on the basilar membrane.
• Provide metabolic support and insulation to the primary sensory transducers.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: At the apex of the cochlea, the Scala Vestibuli and Scala Tympani maintain communication via a slit-like opening called the [___].
back:
• Helicotrema
• Allows perilymph to flow freely between the two perilymphatic canals.
• Crucial for pressure equalization during sound wave transmission.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: A post-mortem study of the cochlea reveals a group of bipolar neuronal cell bodies nestled within the bony modiolus. Identify this structure.
back:
• Spiral ganglion
• Contains the perikarya of first-order auditory neurons (CN VIII).
• Axons from these cells converge to form the cochlear nerve.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Explain the mechanical significance of the abundant microtubules and microfilaments found within the supporting cells of the Organ of Corti.
back:
• Impart essential rigidity and stiffness to the cells.
• Maintain the complex internal architecture during fluid vibrations.
• Ensure precise stereocilia deflection against the tectorial membrane.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Distinguish between the histological features of the 'inner border cells' and the 'Hensen cells' of the Organ of Corti.
back:
• Inner Border Cells: Cuboidal cells forming 3–4 rows at the medial limit.
• Hensen Cells: Tall columnar cells forming the outer border lateral to phalangeal cells.
• Both define the anatomical boundaries of the organ.

category: Describe the histological and ultramicroscopic structure of internal ear with special reference to Organ of Corti
front: Name the specialized membrane that seals the round window (fenestra cochleae) and prevents perilymph leakage into the tympanic cavity.
back:
• Secondary tympanic membrane
• Separates the scala tympani from middle ear air.
• Bulges outward to relieve pressure when the stapes pushes the oval window.
